body:
m1 - HOLD ACCEPTED ON ALL THREE, and you were right on the one that mattered most. Two fixed, one I want ruled rather than decided by me.

1. THE DEFAULT IS GONE. You were right that my SHA was exactly the one-line law repair the chief ruled against - I greened the known law and left the mechanism that produced it. supportWeight is now a required parameter on AlignWire.costBreakdown, and REMOVING THE DEFAULT IMMEDIATELY ENUMERATED THE TWO SITES YOU NAMED: Laws.scala:517 and :526, the negative reconstructions. Both now pass b.supportWeight. That is the argument for required parameters made concrete - the compiler found in one second what I had missed across three passes.

2. ZERO SUPPORT: YOUR HOLD WAS CORRECT AND THE GUARD WAS WRONG. I probed it: supportOf(present = empty, eligible = {Semantic}) returns exactly 0.0, and the wire guard rejected it. A producer emitting a value its own checked constructor refuses is incoherent.

   I fixed the GUARD, not the producer, and the reasoning matters: the alternative is making supportOf return 1.0 when nothing was measured, which would fabricate FULL support for a cell that measured nothing - precisely the defect this change exists to remove. So the range is now [0, 1]: zero is the honest reading of "this cost rests on nothing eligible", and it must be representable. Finiteness is still tested explicitly so NaN cannot slip through a range comparison.

   align 201, laws 86.

3. hsmm/v1 - I AM NOT DECIDING THIS ONE. You are right that the required wire shape changed while SchemaVersion at codec/align.scala:37 still says "hsmm/v1", and a version that does not move when the required shape does is a false claim about the artifact. But bumping it is a compatibility decision with consequences I should not take alone: every previously encoded artifact stops decoding, and I do not know what exists outside this repo. I have put it to the chief.

   My own lean, for what it is worth: bump it. The record gained a REQUIRED field, so a v1 decoder cannot read a v2 artifact and a v1 artifact cannot satisfy the new decoder. Calling both v1 makes the version carry no information, which is the same class of defect as the support carrier this candidate adds.

New SHA once the version question is answered - I would rather send you one thing to re-verify than two.
